hints: Apply Newton's second law to the whole train system up the incline: $DF - (W_{\parallel,E} + W_{\parallel,C}) - (R_E + R_C) = (m_E + m_C)a$.
Calculate weight components: $120000(10)(0.02) = 24000\text{ N}$ and $60000(10)(0.02) = 12000\text{ N}$.
Apply Newton's second law to the coach alone: $T - 12000 - 13000 = 60000(0.3)$ to find $T = 43000\text{ N}$.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law to the combined train system (mass $180000\text{ kg}$) up the incline:
$$DF - (m_E + m_C)g\sin\alpha - (R_E + R_C) = (m_E + m_C)a$$
$$125000 - 180000(10)(0.02) - (22000 + 13000) = 180000a$$
$$125000 - 36000 - 35000 = 180000a$$
$$54000 = 180000a \implies a = \frac{54000}{180000} = 0.3\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the coach alone to find the tension $T$ in the coupling:
$$T - m_C g\sin\alpha - R_C = m_C a$$
$$T - 60000(10)(0.02) - 13000 = 60000(0.3)$$
$$T - 25000 = 18000 \implies T = 43000\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Calculate the gravitational force components parallel to the incline acting down the slope for each vehicle:
For the engine: $W_{\parallel,E} = m_E g\sin\alpha = (120000)(10)(0.02) = 24000\text{ N}$
For the coach: $W_{\parallel,C} = m_C g\sin\alpha = (60000)(10)(0.02) = 12000\text{ N}$

Now consider the coach of mass $60000\text{ kg}$ to determine the coupling tension $T$ pulling it forward:
$$T - W_{\parallel,C} - R_C = m_C a$$
$$T - 12000 - 13000 = (60000)(0.3)$$
$$T - 25000 = 18000$$
$$T = 25000 + 18000 = 43000\text{ N}$$

hints: Calculate the driving force from power and steady speed: $DF = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{4500000}{30} = 150000\text{ N}$.
At steady speed, the net force up the slope is zero: $150000 - 180000g\sin\beta - 35000 = 0$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the driving force of the engine at constant speed $v = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and power $4500\text{ kW}$:
$$DF = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{4500000}{30} = 150000\text{ N}$$

Form the equilibrium equation for the entire train moving at steady speed ($a = 0\text{ m s}^{-2}$) up slope $\beta$:
$$DF - (m_E + m_C)g\sin\beta - (R_E + R_C) = 0$$
$$150000 - 180000(10)\sin\beta - (22000 + 13000) = 0$$
$$115000 = 1800000\sin\beta$$

ai_rubric.Using Power and Resistance Relationships: Finds DF = 150000 N, sets up 150000 - 180000g sin beta - 35000 = 0, and solves for beta = 3.7 deg.

teacher_walkthrough:
Use the relation between mechanical power, driving force, and velocity:
$$P = DF \times v \implies DF = \frac{P}{v}$$

Substitute $P = 4500\text{ kW} = 4500000\text{ W}$ and constant speed $v = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$DF = \frac{4500000}{30} = 150000\text{ N}$$

When moving at a steady speed up an incline of angle $\beta$, acceleration is zero ($a = 0\text{ m s}^{-2}$). The forward driving force balances both the resistance forces and the total component of weight down the slope:
$$DF - (m_E + m_C)g\sin\beta - R_{\text{total}} = 0$$
$$150000 - (180000)(10)\sin\beta - 35000 = 0$$
$$115000 - 1800000\sin\beta = 0$$
$$1800000\sin\beta = 115000$$

Take the inverse sine to find the angle of inclination $\beta$:
$$\beta = \sin^{-1}(0.06388889) \approx 3.6631^\circ$$
$$\beta = 3.7^\circ\quad (\text{to 2 significant figures, or 1 decimal place})$$
